title: The founding of the Shih
summary: How Yi and a temple of monks began the hunt for shen under the Shang.

claims.text: Yi, a Shang noble's son, learned that Yi's own father and other nobles bargained with the Kuei-jin who fed on their people; for calling the father a coward, Yi was exiled with little more than a wagon and arms.
After years among the Chou, Yi rode alone against spider-shen besieging a temple, expecting to die, and survived by a touch of the gods; the monks there became the first Shih.
The Shih learned to turn their will into a weapon and to resist demon tricks through meditation and prayer, and took in survivors who had lost kin to the shen.
Through the river-spirit Heng-O, whom Yi married, Yi learned that not every shen is evil; their five children all became Shih.
Shih study found that silver harms some shen and that jade of various colors guards against others; Yi had warnings carved on bones and shells and left where shen ruled.
The shen answered by using the Shang nobility to send soldiers to kill any shaman outside the corrupt Shang priesthood, while the Chou began to back Yi.
